hyperedges.label: Replacing gh with the GitHub REST API
Output stream discipline: report on stdout, capture and trace on stderr
--update branch state machine (row table, base selection, cleanup, PR create-or-update)

nodes.label: GitHub REST API notes
nodes.rationale: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls with base, head, title, body; .html_url is the line mkprs prints. Reviewers, labels and assignees are separate calls that gh pr create hides behind one invocation, so partial failure becomes possible and reporting success with a warning is preferred over failing the repo. 422 usually means a PR already exists for that head and is a skip, not a failure, which beats the current opaque 'failed to create PR'. Back off on 5xx and on secondary rate limits, which arrive as either 403 or 429, honoring Retry-After when present and falling back to exponential backoff; a 30-repo run trips these.

nodes.label: branchAhead success/skip determination
nodes.rationale: branchAhead measures the branch against origin/<default>, which on a follow-up run is already true from last time, so a no-op command would push and report success. Instead report success only if mkprs pushed code or created a PR; if both already exist on the server it is an earned skip. This also fills a gap: if the command, stage and commit succeed but push or PR creation fails on network/auth, the user gets an automated path to finish after fixing it.

nodes.label: Cleanup can fail silently after a successful run
nodes.source_location: ### Cleanup can fail silently after a successful run
nodes.rationale: High, after --verbose: a repo left somewhere the user did not put it, under a check mark saying everything went fine. repo.restore discards both its errors for git checkout and git branch -D. It stays outcomeSuccess because everything the user asked for happened and cleanup is mkprs tidying up after itself; it gets no summary counter because the three must keep summing to the repo count.
nodes.norm_label: cleanup can fail silently after a successful run

nodes.label: Cleanup restores the branches the repo had
nodes.source_location: #### Cleanup restores the branches the repo had
nodes.rationale: The rule is 'leave the repo with the local branches it started with' rather than 'delete the branch mkprs created', stated so it covers both modes; branchLocation's existing answer is exactly the bit needed. This makes -k a no-op whenever the branch already existed locally (every row 1 and 3 run). It also forecloses a hazard --update would introduce: after -k the repo stands on the branch, so startBranch == branch, repo.restore would no-op the checkout and then try `git branch -D` on the branch it is standing on, which git refuses and the refusal goes unseen because deleteBranch's error is discarded.
nodes.norm_label: cleanup restores the branches the repo had

nodes.label: Delete gitError
nodes.rationale: gitError's only purpose is folding git's first stderr line into an error so a reason line can carry it, which is the thing being ruled out. No production code consumes it (defaultBranch and branchAhead return bool, so the error dies in the helper), and once text echoes stderr under -v the text is available anyway. Keeping it would leave a helper whose only reader is a rule against reading it. Its replacement is a value only the replay reads — failure gaining a detail argument, or run returning the stderr it collected. TestGitErrorCarriesStderr goes with it; TestLoggedErrorDoesNotRepeatStderr asserts the surviving half.

nodes.label: gh → restAPI migration
nodes.rationale: Replace ghCLI outright — restAPI is the only implementation; delete ghArgs and TestGhArgs with it. Keeping both would serve nobody: token source 2 is `gh auth token`, so every user with working gh already hands restAPI a valid token, leaving only users where gh pr create works but gh auth token will not print. Two code paths would disagree on behavior (422 is a skip and a failed reviewer a warning on REST; ghCLI collapses both into 'failed to create PR'), the redaction rule would need getting right twice (argv and method+URL), and a fallback firing only in hard-to-reproduce configurations stays untested until it fails. gh becomes an optional convenience — a place to find a token. The prOpener seam stays, earned by fakePR in the end-to-end tests rather than by having two production implementations.

nodes.label: -i/--interactive review gate
nodes.rationale: Banded Low: the largest item, and --list and --update each deliver a piece of its value far more cheaply. It is `git add -p` for a batch operation, so it borrows that prompt's keys (y/n/p/e/a/q) where they carry over rather than inventing a set. Requires a TTY and fails at startup if stdin is not a terminal so a piped/cron run cannot hang on a keypress it can never receive. stdin is already free because cmd.Stdin is never set in runCommand. The seam is between process's runCommand and commitAndPush calls. `n` is a skip mkprs does not determine for itself, so landing it requires amending the failure/skip note in design-decisions.md.

nodes.label: --list to preview the repo set
nodes.rationale: Medium, first of the band — best value per line left: a flag, an early return and a loop over facts preflight already computes. Covers the 'what would this touch?' half of the old --dry-run that -i does not, since -i still runs the command before it asks.

nodes.label: Make --verbose actually verbose
nodes.rationale: High band, wide shallow work at every git call site. Today -v streams only the user's command's two streams, so it shows the least interesting half of a run and hides the half explaining why a repo failed. Rule: under -v, anything that would help when something goes wrong is on screen as it happens. Gaps: text/ok bypass the capture entirely (originURL, isCleanTree, defaultBranch, branchLocation, resolveBase, headBranch, branchAhead, nothingStaged) even though `status --porcelain` is precisely the list that failed a repo; git's stderr belongs on the -v stream and never appended to a reason line; --quiet flags should stop being passed and the destination decided in one place (repo.log()); `git branch -D`'s stdout carries the only record of what was thrown away; the user's command is echoed with {} already expanded; and the capture moves to stderr in both modes so 2>run.log is a complete diagnostic record. Do not reach for --progress on fetch/push: git suppresses it off a tty for good reason.

nodes.label: Mark the lines that only exist because of -v
nodes.source_location: #### Mark the lines that only exist because of `-v`
nodes.rationale: Every command mkprs runs is printed to stderr prefixed with `$` before it runs — internal git, gh, and the user's command alike — from gitRun.run, the one place every git invocation is built, rather than at each call site. Echo before running so a hang is attributable to the line above it. Quote arguments that would otherwise read as several, since the commit message defaults to the command text; {} expansion happens first because it is the only part that varies between repos. Trace lines go straight to stderr and never into c.buf, so the buffer keeps exactly what the user's command emitted and the two verbosities cannot disagree. No replay under -v, since a failure already streamed live and reprinting would double it. prOpener.open should take the capture rather than an io.Writer, because only the implementation knows its own invocation and a plain writer cannot distinguish a trace line from narrated output — and it puts the redaction constraint on the side of the seam that can honor it.
nodes.norm_label: mark the lines that only exist because of -v

nodes.label: Opening versus updating the pull request
nodes.source_location: #### Opening versus updating the pull request
nodes.rationale: openPR becomes create-or-return-existing and must tell the caller which, since that plus whether anything was pushed determines skip versus success. pipeline.go's commitAndPush splits into independent commit and push, with push returning whether it did anything separate from err. `gh pr create` fails when a PR exists for the head branch, so it needs a `gh pr view --json url` fallback until the 422 handling under API notes replaces it. Title and body are left alone: the PR describes the whole effort, each commit its increment, and a human-edited title must not be overwritten; --title/--body/--reviewers/--draft apply only on the create path and should say so rather than being silently ignored. Report created versus updated apart via an `updated bool` and a second constructor beside success, keeping the three summary counters so they still sum to the repo count.
nodes.norm_label: opening versus updating the pull request

nodes.label: Per-repo command timeout, defaulting to 10 minutes
nodes.source_location: ### Per-repo command timeout, defaulting to 10 minutes
nodes.rationale: High, do this first. One hung command stalls the whole run with no feedback, and serial execution means it stalls every repo behind it. exec.CommandContext with context.WithTimeout in runCommand; expiry is a normal per-repo failure so the run continues and cleanup fires through the existing defer a.cleanup. Ships with a default on like --max-repos, because a limit you have to remember to pass is absent exactly when it matters — nobody types --timeout on the run where the command turns out to hang. 10 minutes sits clear of a slow-but-real npm ci or dotnet restore while still catching a wedged process the same afternoon.
nodes.norm_label: per-repo command timeout, defaulting to 10 minutes

nodes.label: Priority bands (High / Medium / Low)
nodes.rationale: Every item carries a band so the order is decided once rather than re-argued each session. Rules in order: security and bugs before features; prerequisites above what they unblock; value against effort; safety nets outrank their size because they bound a failure landing in other people's repositories. Order within a band is loose; the band is the commitment, and an item with no band is one nobody has decided about yet.

nodes.label: Refuse the default branch, before any repo is touched
nodes.source_location: #### Refuse the default branch, before any repo is touched
nodes.rationale: `mkprs ~/repos -b main` is harmless today only because every repo fails on 'branch already exists'; under --update the same typo would commit and push to main across the fleet. It is a startup error like an uninterpretable target, not a per-repo failure, and not part of the continue table which would happily say continue.
nodes.norm_label: refuse the default branch, before any repo is touched

nodes.label: Replace gh with direct GitHub API calls
nodes.source_location: ## Replace `gh` with direct GitHub API calls
nodes.rationale: Medium, high work and high reward: gh is the last external binary, which undercuts the reason mkprs was written in Go — download one file and run it on any platform. Opening a PR is a few REST requests, so it costs net/http calls and an auth story with no new dependencies. The seam already exists: ghCLI implements prOpener in internal/mkprs/pr.go, so a restAPI drops in without touching openPR, and end-to-end tests inject fakePR. New tests use red/green TDD and standard Go interception rather than calling GitHub.
nodes.norm_label: replace gh with direct github api calls

nodes.label: e — drop into a shell in the repo
nodes.source_location: #### `e` — drop into a shell in the repo
nodes.rationale: The payoff of the interactive feature: a codemod handling 90% of repos leaves a handful needing a human, and today that means aborting and starting over. Launch $SHELL falling back to /bin/sh (%COMSPEC%/powershell on Windows), cwd at the repo root, passing the real terminal through — the deliberate exception to /dev/null stdin and captured output, because a shell that cannot see its tty is useless and the user's session must not end up in a replayed capture. Exit code ignored because people type `exit 1` out of habit. Re-read the diff afterwards, never cache it, so a full revert falls through to the usual no-changes skip. A `git checkout` inside the shell fails the repo by the same rule as the command. Deliberately does not touch --max-repos or the timeout: prompting on the count turns a circuit breaker into a reflexive y, and prompting on a timeout replaces fail-and-move-on with block-forever.
nodes.norm_label: e — drop into a shell in the repo

nodes.label: Token discovery and authentication
nodes.rationale: Order, first hit wins: GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN (the CI convention gh reads first, though Actions requires mapping the token into env); `gh auth token` if gh is on PATH, inheriting gh's keyring/hosts.yml without reimplementing it; `git credential fill` reaching the platform credential helper git push already relies on; otherwise fail with an actionable message naming all three. First hit wins even when the API rejects it, because falling through on a 401 would make which identity opened a PR depend on which credential happened to be expired. The cost is that a rejected token looks like a bare 'bad credentials' with three plausible culprits, so the token's source is carried alongside it and named in every auth failure. The token authenticates the API, not git push, which introduces two failure modes gh masked (SSH-only user with no token; token set with no push credentials), so fetch the token early and fail before any repo is touched. Never let the token reach disk, ps, or the capture — a failed repo replays its capture verbatim. Derive the host from remote.origin.url for GHES rather than hardcoding api.github.com; originURL already reads the un-rewritten config value.

nodes.label: --tracked-only staging
nodes.rationale: Medium, last of the band. `git add -A` is the right default because tools like dotnet outdated -u and scaffolders create files, but a command dropping build artifacts into a repo with a thin .gitignore will commit them; --tracked-only stages with `git add -u`.

nodes.label: --update to add to an existing branch and PR
nodes.source_location: ### `--update` to add to an existing branch and PR
nodes.rationale: Medium band, highest value and largest change. Today preflight fails every repo with 'branch already exists on origin', which reads like a guardrail but is the tool declining to help. --update means create-or-update: adopt the branch where it exists, create it where it does not, so a repo dirty on the first run is picked up by the same re-run. Distinct from the rejected 'just open the PR' mode because it still runs the command in every repo and so scales identically. Never implicit: the flag is the whole safety story, since silently adopting a matching branch is the trap.
nodes.norm_label: --update to add to an existing branch and pr

nodes.label: --update when-to-continue row table
nodes.rationale: Pure git, no GitHub query, evaluated on refs/heads and refs/remotes/origin after preflight's fetch --prune. Every yes row needs no ref moved and every no row would: rows 1 and 3 already sit on the starting commit so a plain checkout suffices; rows 5 and 6 create a local branch, which is not a move; rows 2 and 4 would need checkout -B. Equality tests are exact rather than 'is an ancestor of', because widening would quietly reintroduce the -B the table exists to avoid. Row 2 covers behind (would require a pull) and ahead (would push unintended work), both resolved by manual intervention. Row 4 protects un-pushed work as a side effect, since git cannot distinguish a squash-merged deleted branch from genuine local work and only the PR's state could — which would make prOpener report state rather than a URL. Every no row is a failure, not a skip, naming the branch and what would unblock it. A squash-merged PR in a repo that does not auto-delete lands in row 1 and preflight should detect the divergence and fail.

nodes.label: Where the branch starts from, by row
nodes.source_location: #### Where the branch starts from, by row
nodes.rationale: process checks out -b <branch> <base> unconditionally today; under --update rows 1 and 3 become plain `checkout <branch>`, row 5 creates from origin/<branch>, row 6 creates from origin/<default> as today. So prep.base becomes row-dependent rather than always resolveBase's answer — the main structural change --update makes to process.
nodes.norm_label: where the branch starts from, by row

nodes.label: Working agreement
nodes.rationale: Pick items by the priority rules rather than first-in-list; use red/green TDD so the test is validated and behavior defined before implementation; comments explain why and name the losing alternative; one item at a time; ask rather than assume; completed items are deleted rather than marked done; design-decisions.md is edited only when a standing truth changes.

nodes.label: The capture holds the user's workflow, not mkprs's bookkeeping
nodes.source_location: ## The capture holds the user's workflow, not mkprs's bookkeeping
nodes.rationale: mkprs automates a manual routine (fetch, branch, run command, stage, commit, push, open PR) and what those emit is what the user would have seen by hand, so it is captured and replayed on failure. What mkprs runs to decide what to do stays out: the user never typed it and its failures are answers rather than errors. The rule is intent, not a list, so a step added later classifies itself. --verbose is where both appear.
nodes.norm_label: the capture holds the user's workflow, not mkprs's bookkeeping

nodes.label: The command must leave the repo on mkprs's branch
nodes.source_location: ## The command must leave the repo on mkprs's branch
nodes.rationale: Committing acts on HEAD, so a `git checkout` inside the user command would commit to a branch mkprs does not own, or push to main. Any branch switch, and a detached HEAD, fails the repo.
nodes.norm_label: the command must leave the repo on mkprs's branch

nodes.label: Discovery finds only outermost, non-linked repos
nodes.source_location: ## Discovery finds only outermost, non-linked repos
nodes.rationale: Only repos containing a .git *folder* qualify. Submodules and worktrees are excluded because dedupeRepos keys on path, so a worktree of an already-found repo would not dedupe, producing two branches and two PRs against one GitHub repo. A repo's subtree is pruned once found so nested repos are never walked into.
nodes.norm_label: discovery finds only outermost, non-linked repos

nodes.label: Execution stays serial
nodes.rationale: No -j/--jobs. Serial execution lets a failure replay its capture as one contiguous block, keeps result lines one-per-line without a mutex, and makes --verbose readable. Most batch commands are fast enough that wall-clock saving does not pay for the complexity. Revisit only with evidence of a genuinely slow run.

nodes.label: A failed repo is not cleaned up at all
nodes.source_location: ## A failed repo is not cleaned up at all
nodes.rationale: Cleanup is all or nothing because checking out the default branch drags the command's uncommitted edits along with it. Failures leave branch, commits and working tree as they are; skips still clean up. Same reason there is nothing between -k and full cleanup.
nodes.norm_label: a failed repo is not cleaned up at all

nodes.label: A failure is a repo you will have to run again for
nodes.source_location: ## A failure is a repo you will have to run again for
nodes.rationale: Success is a pull request; skip is earned only when mkprs determined definitively there was no PR to create; anything else that stops a repo is a failure (unreachable origin, failing user command, dirty tree, detached HEAD, no discoverable default branch, branch already present). Not being able to tell whether there was anything to do is itself a failure. Consequently a failure's reason line says what would unblock it, the exit code restates rather than decides this, and --stop-on-failure stops because a wrong command and a wrong starting state both cost a second run.
nodes.norm_label: a failure is a repo you will have to run again for

nodes.label: mkprs never moves a branch to a commit it did not create
nodes.source_location: ## mkprs never moves a branch to a commit it did not create
nodes.rationale: No pull, merge, rebase or reset in internal/mkprs. A stale local main is read around, never updated, because repositioning a ref destroys silently and unattended across forty repos.
nodes.norm_label: mkprs never moves a branch to a commit it did not create

nodes.label: No "I did manual work, just open the PR" mode
nodes.source_location: ## No "I did manual work, just open the PR" mode
nodes.rationale: Easily done with `gh pr create` in a loop, bypasses most of what mkprs does, pushes code it did not create, and adds a lot of complexity for little gain.
nodes.norm_label: no "i did manual work, just open the pr" mode

nodes.label: PRs always target the repo's own default branch
nodes.source_location: ## PRs always target the repo's own default branch
nodes.rationale: No --pr-base flag: base and fork point must agree so the diff is exactly the commit the run made.
nodes.norm_label: prs always target the repo's own default branch

nodes.label: stdout is the report; stderr is everything else
nodes.source_location: ## stdout is the report; stderr is everything else
nodes.rationale: stdout carries what mkprs concluded (result lines, summary, --help); errors, discarded-target notices, command capture and all of --verbose go to stderr. A failure's capture is stderr too even though it replays under a stdout line, so redirecting stdout leaves a readable report rather than one broken up by forty commands' worth of output.
nodes.norm_label: stdout is the report; stderr is everything else

nodes.label: A target is a repo or a place to find them
nodes.source_location: ## A target is a repo or a place to find them, never a place inside one
nodes.rationale: A subfolder of a repo stops the run because the intent is unambiguous but the unit of work is wrong, and silently widening it to the whole repo is not mkprs's call. A target that neither is nor contains a repo is ignored rather than fatal (globs like ~/repos/* sweeping a notes/ folder are ordinary) but still reported so an empty glob does not read as a run with nothing to do. Per-directory work is rejected because it would make the directory rather than the repo the unit of work, which is the spine of outcome, reporting and commits; `-- bash -c 'cd src && ...'` costs nothing. Revisit only with a repo where that is painful.
nodes.norm_label: a target is a repo or a place to find them

nodes.label: Tests use real git, not a faked one
nodes.source_location: ## Tests use real `git`, not a faked one
nodes.rationale: No gitRunner interface: git is not a boundary but where mkprs's behavior lives, and a fake written from the same understanding as the code passes on the same wrong understanding. prOpener earns its seam because gh needs network, credentials, and eventually multiple implementations.
nodes.norm_label: tests use real git, not a faked one
